idea-plugin.name: Terminal Safety Rails
idea-plugin.description:
Terminal Safety Rails — Intercept Dangerous Commands Before Execution

A single destructive command can ruin your day. Terminal Safety Rails intercepts dangerous commands like rm -rf, kubectl delete, and terraform destroy before they execute — showing a risk-level confirmation dialog that requires explicit approval.

NEW in 2026.5: Cloud & Database Guardrails

  • Cloud Infrastructure Protection — intercepts destructive AWS, GCP and Azure CLI operations before they run: aws s3 rb, aws ec2 terminate-instances, aws rds delete-db-instance, aws cloudformation delete-stack, gsutil rm -r, gcloud … delete, az group delete and more
  • SQL Mass-Mutation Guard — catches the classic data-loss footgun: DELETE FROM / UPDATE … SET with no WHERE clause, statement-scoped so a safe query never masks an unscoped one — including statements embedded in psql -c / mysql -e
  • Cloud & SQL Safer Alternatives — list-before-delete, stop-instead-of-terminate, describe-first, SELECT-preview and transaction-wrapped mutations, copy-pasteable right in the dialog

Understand, Don't Just Approve

  • Command Explainer — the dialog tells you in plain English what the command will actually do, with every dangerous flag decoded (rm, git, kubectl, docker, terraform, chmod, dd, find, mkfs, kill…)
  • Safer Alternatives — copy-pasteable safer equivalents right in the dialog: --force-with-lease, dry runs, backups first, least-privilege chmod
  • Shell History Risk Audit — score your whole ~/.zsh_history with a 0–100 safety score, risk distribution and the riskiest commands (MD/JSON/HTML export + headless CLI for security onboarding)
  • Enforcement Modes — Warn only / Confirm / Block critical / Lockdown (auto-block HIGH+ during production freezes; fully audited)

Command Interception

  • 33 Built-in Rules — Covers filesystem, Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker, AWS/GCP/Azure cloud, Git, SQL, system services, and permissions
  • 13 Heuristic Detectors — A 0–100 risk score independent of the rules: destructive file ops, privilege escalation, shell injection, remote code execution, credential exposure, network exfiltration, production targets, disk wipes, fork bombs, git history rewrites, privileged package managers, cloud destruction, and unscoped SQL mutations
  • 4 Risk Levels — CRITICAL (red), HIGH (orange), MEDIUM (yellow), LOW (green) with color-coded dialogs
  • Confirmation Dialog — Shows matched command, risk level, category, and explanation before execution
  • Zero overhead for safe commands — Only dangerous patterns trigger the dialog

Customization

  • Custom Rules — Add your own patterns with glob or regex matching and configurable risk levels
  • Team-Shared Rules — Share rules via .terminal-safety-rules.yaml in your project root
  • Enable/Disable Toggle — Quickly turn protection on and off
  • Unlimited Custom Rules — No cap on custom command patterns
  • Context-Aware Detection — Smarter matching based on environment
  • Audit Log — Track all intercepted commands with timestamps and actions
  • Command Statistics — Analytics on intercepted commands and usage patterns

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.3+ (or any JetBrains IDE based on IntelliJ Platform)
  • Terminal plugin (bundled with JetBrains IDEs)
  • Java 17+

Support

  • Issue Tracker
  • Documentation
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2026.5.0

  • Cloud Infrastructure Protection - Intercepts destructive AWS/GCP/Azure CLI commands before they run: aws s3 rb, aws ec2 terminate-instances, aws rds delete-db-instance, aws dynamodb delete-table, aws cloudformation delete-stack, aws eks delete-cluster, gcloud … delete, gsutil rm -r, az group delete (new Cloud category, 10 new rules + a heuristic detector)
  • SQL Mass-Mutation Guard - Catches DELETE FROM / UPDATE … SET with no WHERE clause — statement-scoped so a safe query never masks an unscoped one, and works inside psql -c / mysql -e invocations
  • Cloud & SQL Safer Alternatives - The dialog now offers list-before-delete, stop-instead-of-terminate, describe-first, SELECT-preview and transaction-wrapped mutations
  • 33 built-in rules and 13 heuristic detectors (up from 23 rules / 11 detectors)
  • 398 unit tests, 0 failures

2026.4.0

  • Safer Alternatives - The confirmation dialog now offers copy-pasteable safer equivalents (git push --force-with-lease, kubectl --dry-run=client, terraform plan -destroy, backups before DROP DATABASE, and more)
  • Command Explainer - Plain-English "What will this do?" with decoded dangerous flags, right in the dialog
  • Shell History Risk Audit - Score your whole shell history (zsh/bash) with a 0-100 safety score, risk distribution, riskiest commands and MD/JSON/HTML exports; headless CLI with --fail-below gate
  • Enforcement Modes - Warn only / Confirm / Block critical / Lockdown: auto-block HIGH and CRITICAL findings during production freezes, fully recorded in the audit log
  • Fixed - Marketplace publish token environment variable mismatch (PUBLISH_TOKEN vs PLUGIN_TOKEN)
  • 344 unit tests, 0 failures

Earlier

  • Command Interception - Catches dangerous terminal commands before execution and shows a confirmation dialog
  • 4 Risk Levels - Color-coded CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW severity ratings for each intercepted command
  • 23 Built-in Rules - Pre-configured patterns covering filesystem, Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker, Git, SQL, system services, and permissions
  • Custom Rules - Add your own dangerous command patterns with glob or regex matching and configurable risk levels
  • Color-Coded Confirmation Dialog - Visual warning dialog showing the matched command, risk level, and explanation of why the command is dangerous
  • Team-Shared Rules - Share safety rules across your team via a .terminal-safety-rules.yaml file in your project root
  • Context-Aware Detection - Smarter matching based on the current environment and context
  • Audit Log - Track all intercepted commands with timestamps and actions taken
  • Command Statistics - Analytics on intercepted commands and team usage patterns
